requests.status: Closed by the City: no responsive documents
requests.asked: Water, wastewater and power agreements with Amp Z; any proposed or signed Chapter 380 or 381 incentive agreements; studies of the project’s water use and power needs; and correspondence about utility capacity and “take-or-pay” water clauses.

events.text: Request emailed to the City Secretary. This was ETLC’s first public records request.
The City asked that requests be submitted through its official channels.
Request refiled through the City’s public information address.
The City said that after a reasonable search it found no responsive documents, said information about economic development negotiations was excepted under Sec. 552.131, and closed the request.

requests.asked: The industrial development ordinance adopted in August 2026; city limits and ETJ maps for both sites; water, sewer and utility agreements with the companies; records of the City's wells on the former Southland Paper Mill property; the documents behind the 500-gallons-a-day figure in the City's Data Center FAQ; communications with the companies; and records of the Nov. 7, 2025 meeting and any letters of support signed by City officials.

events.text: Request filed and logged by the City.
City sent a cost estimate of $108 and asked for a $54 deposit.

City asked the Texas Attorney General to let it withhold records, citing economic development negotiations (Sec. 552.131), internal policy advice (Sec. 552.111) and possible third-party business information (Sec. 552.110).
ETLC accepted the estimate and asked the City to release the records it did not send to the Attorney General.
ETLC paid the $54 deposit in cash at the City Secretary's Office and received a receipt.

requests.waiting: The Attorney General's ruling, due by about mid-December 2026, and release of the records the City did not submit for review.

requests.asked: The City's water system records: an inventory of City wells with production and water-level records since 2016; water and wastewater capacity and demand since 2021; water, wastewater and capital plans; any study of serving a data center or other large industrial water user; any will-serve letter or capacity reservation for the companies; how the City would supply and charge for that water at the former mill; and the City's 2009 purchase of the mill's water system.

events.text: Request filed and logged by the City.
City asked for a $234 deposit, half of its estimated charges.
City included the parts of this request that overlap CRR-2026-315 in its request to the Attorney General.
ETLC asked the City to remove the parts that overlap CRR-2026-315 and to send a revised itemized statement with the total, and pointed out records already available online that could be dropped.

At the City's request, ETLC marked the items to remove: City well locations, Pineywoods permits and production reports, water system capacity and demand, wastewater capacity and flows, the capital improvement plan, and the drought and conservation plans. ETLC asked for a revised itemized statement with the total and a written response to its fee waiver request.

requests.waiting: A revised itemized statement from the City and a written response to the fee waiver request.

clock.start_note: ETLC marked the items to remove

requests.asked: Incentive offers, letters of intent and nondisclosure agreements with the companies; site marketing materials for the former Southland mill and Northern Chip Mill sites; records of the Nov. 7, 2025 meeting; letters of support; board agendas and minutes mentioning data centers; and correspondence about the project.

events.text: Request sent to the EDC and logged by the City.

City said five of the seven items duplicate CRR-2026-315 and are handled there. For site marketing materials and for board agendas and minutes mentioning data centers, it said it found no responsive records.

requests.waiting: Nothing further; the overlapping records follow CRR-2026-315.

requests.asked: Well permit applications for Amp Z, Verdant Industries or anyone seeking groundwater at the former Southland Paper Mill site; correspondence with those companies since 2024; any well application in Angelina County since 2024 for more than 25,000 gallons a day; and board agendas and minutes discussing them.

events.text: Request filed.

The District answered in writing: no well applications near the Southland mill site in the past two years and no contact with Amp Z or Verdant. It disclosed that WattBridge was approved in late 2024 and early 2025 for a well permit of 80 million gallons a year for a power plant in the north of the county, never drilled, and in March 2026 asked for 1.5 billion gallons a year for a 24/7 plant; that request has been on hold since July 2026 at the company's request. The District asked whether ETLC still wanted the documents and requested until Oct. 16 to gather them.
ETLC confirmed it still wants the WattBridge permit applications and the related board agendas and minutes, and dropped the rig supply well applications.

requests.waiting: The WattBridge permit applications and the related board agendas and minutes.

clock.start_note: ETLC confirmed which records it still wants

requests.asked: District rules and management plan; well permits and applications for wells on or serving either site; production records; any permit to export groundwater; board minutes and agendas mentioning data centers or the companies; and correspondence with the companies.

events.text: Request filed.
District sent its rules, the expired permits for three wells at the Ben Dunn Road site, board minutes and agendas, and an email exchange with agents for the site, and asked clarifying questions.
ETLC answered the questions and listed the records still needed. The District said its management plan is posted on its website and that pulling the rest will take time.

requests.waiting: The remaining well, permit and correspondence records.

clock.start_note: ETLC answered the District's clarifying questions

requests.asked: Any road use agreement with the companies; tax abatement applications, drafts and reinvestment zone records for either site, including the Long Leaf Generating LLC abatement approved in May 2025; Resolution 010-26; county permits for either site; records of the Oncor easement to Exacore LLC filed May 13, 2025; correspondence with the companies; records of the Nov. 7, 2025 meeting; and letters of support.

events.text: Request sent to the County Judge's office and Commissioners Court.
After ETLC paid the County's $45 charge, County Judge Keith Wright's office sent its records.
Commissioner Kermit Kennedy (Precinct 2) also forwarded records.

requests.waiting: Nothing further. ETLC is reviewing the County's records.

requests.asked: The approved minutes of the Feb. 9, 2026 Planning and Zoning meeting; the Feb. 23, 2026 special meeting packet; recordings and sign-in sheets; staff and commissioner communications from Feb. 9 to 23 about public comment procedures or the data center; and records showing whether the Feb. 23 packet was ever posted online.

events.text: Request emailed to the City Secretary and the City’s public information address.

The City released records: the Data Center FAQ email sent to Planning and Zoning commissioners on Feb. 9, commission agendas and minutes, the bylaws, the Feb. 23 sign-in sheet, and audio recordings of the Feb. 9 and Feb. 23 meetings.

requests.waiting: ETLC is checking the City's Oct. 23 release against the request.
